subject: Harmonize auto-renew & off-ramp timing — proposed compromise for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <contracts@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redlines — remove auto-renew & shorten notice window

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close on commercial terms, but legal has pushed back hard on the auto-renew clause in the MSA and wants a much shorter termination notice (30 days) for renewal and termination-for-convenience. They want the ability to opt out without a long notice window given our procurement calendar.

Attached is the redline that Acme Legal submitted (highlighted items are the priorities). Can Redwood accept removal of auto-renew entirely and a 30-day out for all Order Forms? If not, please propose an alternative.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Head of Contracts, Acme Analytics
[Attachment: Acme_MSA_redline_LG.pdf (pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <contracts@acme-analytics.com>, Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — remove auto-renew & shorten notice window

Thanks Lina — appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can't remove auto-renew across the board for enterprise Order Forms (predictability for committed capacity is key), but we can propose a pragmatic middle ground that responds to Acme's concerns while protecting capacity commitments for Dedicated/Dedicated+ tiers.

Proposed compromise (summary):
- Keep auto-renew for committed Dedicated capacity but move from "automatic 12-month renew" to an opt-in auto-renew with a 60-day advance cancellation window for Dedicated customers (we'll still bill unless notice is provided).
- For Hosted/Pay-as-you-go Order Forms, offer a 30-day notice and no auto-renew.
- Add a pilot carve-out: Order Forms flagged as "Pilot" get a 30-day out and no auto-renew regardless of capacity.
- Add a limited termination-for-convenience fee for early exit from committed Dedicated capacity (one-quarter of remaining committed months) — refundable if termination is Redwood-initiated.

I have attached an internal redline showing our proposed language to start the conversation. If this looks reasonable, Aditya can present the compromise to Lina and Brian, and Karthik can confirm whether the proposed termination fee and carve-out language are acceptable to Legal.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal legal review (Karthik) on proposed redline and fee mechanics.
2) Sales (Aditya) to present at decision meeting this Friday (12/04) and capture Acme feedback.
3) If Acme tentatively agrees, we prepare a clean Order Form and route for signatures via DocuSign.

Thanks — talk soon.

Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_Redwood_proposed_redline_kp.docx (docx)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — remove auto-renew & shorten notice window

Kimberly / Aditya — reviewed the proposed compromise. High-level feedback from Legal:
- We can accept tiered auto-renew mechanics (no auto-renew for Hosted / Pilot; opt-in auto-renew for Dedicated with notice) if the Order Form clearly states the capacity commit and the consequences of early termination.
- The termination-for-convenience fee needs clearer caps and a reconciliation mechanism so it doesn't count as a penalty. Suggest: fee = pro-rated remaining commitment * 25%, but offset by any reallocation credit if Redwood can reassign the reserved capacity within 90 days. That reduces Acme's exposure and keeps commercial fairness.
- For notice windows, we should avoid <30 days for any committed capacity. 30 days is risky for Dedicated ramp-downs; 60 days is reasonable for Dedicated and 30 for Hosted/pilot.

Actionable redline suggestions I added inline in the attached doc. Also recommend we include a special "procurement freeze" clause for the first 90 days post-signature for any committed capacity so both sides have a short ramp/lock-in window.

I'll mark the legal-approved passages in the next version.

-Karthik
General Counsel (contracts lead)
[Attachment: MSA_Redline_Legal_karthik_vA.docx (docx)]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — remove auto-renew & shorten notice window

Team — I'll take point with Acme. My suggested negotiation play: lead with the pilot carve-out + Hosted 30-day no-auto-renew; position Dedicated as a fixed-commit resource where predictable pricing requires an opt-in auto-renew or a limited exit fee.

Talking points for customer call (Friday 12/04):
- Explain operational reason for auto-renew on Dedicated (capacity allocation, GPU reservations).
- Offer the 25% pro-rated early termination fee with the 90-day reallocation offset (per Karthik).
- Guarantee a "good faith" attempt to reassign freed capacity and a cap on fees if reallocation occurs quickly.
- Offer to add an internal SLA credit if Redwood initiates a change that materially affects Acme's capacity within the first 6 months.

I'll record the meeting notes in HubSpot and update the draft redline after the call.

Aditya
Account Executive — Strategic Sales

[Internal note: bring the revised redline and the summary slide showing the compromise — helps execs approve concessions quickly.]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <contracts@acme-analytics.com>, Brian O'Neill <brian.oneill@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — remove auto-renew & shorten notice window

Lina / Brian — thanks for your patience and for the frank redlines. Following internal review here is a concise proposal to resolve the primary concerns you raised:

1) Pilot and Hosted Order Forms: No auto-renew. 30-day termination/renewal notice.
2) Dedicated (committed capacity): Auto-renew remains available as an opt-in on the Order Form. If Acme opts into auto-renew, Redwood requires 60 days' notice to cancel. If Acme opts out, then a pro-rated early-termination fee applies for the remainder of the committed term equal to 25% of remaining committed fees, offset by reallocation credit if we reassign capacity within 90 days.
3) Procurement freeze: For any committed capacity, a 90-day lock/transition window post-signature to stabilize deployment (no unilateral immediate cancellation).

We've attached the redline that integrates Legal's edits and the termination fee mechanics. If this looks acceptable, Aditya will prepare an updated Order Form and route via DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm whether Acme will accept the Dedicated opt-in approach or requires a complete removal of auto-renew (we can then escalate).
- We: finalize the redline (legal + sales) and share a clean Order Form + DocuSign envelope by 12/11.

Thanks and happy to jump on a call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_Acme_final_proposal_redline_20261209.docx (docx)]
